member.name: T:Regalis.API.Auditing.AuditOutcome
member.summary:
Builds the audit row for a request that did NOT go through: Failed (validation error, exception) or Denied (missing permission, business rule) — Audit Trail Enhancements §5.3. Successful changes are audited by the save-changes interceptor; this covers the attempts that never reach a save, so blocked and failed operations are visible too.
What was attempted is inferred from the endpoint: HTTP verb and action name give the action, the controller gives the entity, the route's id gives the entity ID. The JSON body the caller sent (secrets stripped) is kept as the "After" the user tried to save.

member.name: T:Regalis.API.Authorization.RequireCompleteProfileAttribute
member.summary:
Refuses an action until the caller has finished onboarding.
The SPA redirects an incomplete member to the onboarding form, but a redirect is not a control — anyone can call the API directly. This is the part that holds, and it goes on the endpoints that cannot do their job without the missing data: anything raising an invoice needs a billing address and a GSTIN.
An AUTHORIZATION filter, not an action filter, for two reasons. It runs before model binding and validation, so an incomplete member is told to finish their profile rather than being handed a validation error about a payload that was never going to be accepted. And it means a malformed body cannot be used to probe past the gate.
Read-only endpoints are deliberately left open, so an incomplete member can still see their account instead of meeting a wall everywhere. Staff and admins are never blocked — User.IsProfileComplete treats them as complete by definition.

member.name: T:Regalis.API.Authorization.StaffOnlyAttribute
member.summary:
Refuses customer logins on an admin-portal endpoint, whatever permissions their token carries.
Permissions alone cannot separate the portals: a customer legitimately holds WALLET.VIEW and QUOTATION.VIEW for their OWN wallet and quotations, and those same codes guard the admin screens that read EVERY customer's. Without this filter, one customer could read another's wallet ledger (/api/wallet/{id}, /api/admin/wallets/{id}) or quotations (GET /api/quotations) — found 2026-09-28. Put it on any route whose data spans customers; the customer portal keeps its own "my" routes.
An authorization filter, so it runs before model binding, like RequireCompleteProfile.

member.name: T:Regalis.API.Controllers.PurchaseOrdersController
member.summary:
Purchase orders (document §4). Draft → PendingApproval → Approved → Sent → (Partially) Received, Cancelled until goods arrive. A PO is editable only while Draft, and receiving goods against it writes the incoming inventory rows in the same transaction — there is no separate goods-received endpoint that could drift.
Permissions: VIEW reads, prints and downloads; CREATE raises, attaches files and submits; EDIT changes a draft and records receipts; APPROVE approves, rejects and sends; DELETE cancels.

member.name: T:Regalis.API.Controllers.QuotationsController
member.summary:
Quotations (document §6–§8). Both portals are served here: the admin routes manage the quotation, the "my" routes are the customer's own view and their approve/reject decision. Customer routes are scoped by ICurrentUser inside the service, so the id in the URL can never reach another customer's quotation.
Every state rule the screen shows as a greyed-out button is enforced again here: a sent quotation cannot be edited, only the newest revision can be approved, and a quotation converts to an invoice once and only from Approved.

member.name: T:Regalis.API.UtcDateTimeConverter
member.summary: Every DateTime in this system is UTC (A13), but values materialized from SQL Server carry DateTimeKind.Unspecified and would serialize without the Z suffix, which browsers then parse as local time. This converter stamps Unspecified as UTC on the way out and normalizes inbound values to UTC.
